Forecast Discussion

High pressure over the Southern Appalachians gives us two warm, dry days. A dry front arrives from the north Friday night. The weekend is cooler with more clouds--back to normal for late October: nice enough, just not the “glory days” of late. A little drizzle is possible Sunday night into early Monday.

Temperatures moderate a little Monday and Tuesday. Drizzle is possible again Tuesday night, but significant rain holds off until later Wednesday and Thursday.

Low pressure is over northern Arkansas Wednesday morning with a front extending southeastward into the Mississippi Delta. The low moves to west Tennessee by Thursday morning and forces lots of moisture into the Southern Appalachians. Wednesday, light rain or drizzle is possible from morning into afternoon, then rain arrives from the south late in the day or evening. Rain may be heavy at times after midnight Wednesday night and into Thursday. This is our first significant rain since early October.
